sources.text:
ROCHESTER, Minn. (KTTC) – KTTC is fact-checking claims made during Wednesday night’s Minnesota gubernatorial debate. The debate was hosted live by KTTC in partnership with Minnesota’s Gray Media stations and FOX 9. Election Day is less than 13 days away.

###### WATCH THE FULL DEBATE

## Klobuchar on federal prosecutors

Sen. Amy Klobuchar said she worked with the Department of Justice following the 2022 Feeding Our Future fraud indictments to secure additional federal prosecutors for Minnesota.

KTTC rated this claim true. It was validated by then-U.S. Attorney Andy Luger, who said it was the largest national increase among U.S. attorneys’ offices at the time.

KTTC fact check(KTTC)

## Demuth on fraud under state leaders’ watch

Speaker Lisa Demuth accused her opponent of doing nothing on fraud in Minnesota. Demuth said Minnesota leaders allowed $9 billion in fraud to happen under their watch.

KTTC rated this claim as needing context. The $9 billion figure was taken from a statement made by then-acting U.S. Attorney Joe Thompson, who said in December that half of the $18 billion paid out from certain Medicaid programs over a five-year period could be fraudulent. The Department of Justice has not provided documentation to back up that claim as it continues to investigate fraud in Minnesota.

KTTC fact check(KTTC)

## Demuth on Keystone XL pipeline capacity

Demuth said the canceled Keystone XL pipeline would have transported up to 830,000 barrels of oil per day.

KTTC rated this claim true. The project was canceled by the Biden administration in 2021, citing environmental concerns. The pipeline was to run from western Canada to refineries in the Gulf Coast. President Trump has suggested reviving the pipeline.

KTTC fact check(KTTC)

## Klobuchar on health care coverage losses

Klobuchar claimed 8 million Americans lost their health care coverage last year because of Trump administration Medicaid cuts and the expiration of the ACA tax credits.

KTTC rated this claim as needing context. The 8 million figure is from the Democrat House Committee on the Budget. According to a June 2026 report from the Department of Health and Human Services, some of the coverage losses can be tied to efforts to root out fraud and abuse.

KTTC fact check(KTTC)

KTTC will continue fact-checking Wednesday’s debate.

Watch the full debate right here: 2026 Minnesota Gubernatorial Debate - Amy Klobuchar and Lisa Demuth
